correctness.rationale: Re-derived the zero-mean two-phase stationarity equations and potential U_K: Hessian/K=diag(w1 cos(alpha),w2 cos(beta))+a cos(alpha-beta)[[1,-1],[-1,1]]. For K>=K0, negative chord cosine at an interior stationary point implies the strict rank-one update bound cot(A+B)(tan(A/2)+tan(B/2))<1; thus Hessian positive definite even under frustration. At K>K0 all four boundary gradients point outwards and degree +1 counts the unique interior stable lock. At K=K0, all unsaturated faces admit inward descent; opposite-sign saturated corners have energy variation K0(w1+w2)(t-sin t)+K0 a(cos(2t)-1)<0 for small t, giving an interior strict lock and continuation below K0 unless leaf loads are aligned. In the aligned case summing leaf equations forces K>=K0 for every torus lock. Direct independent substitution at w1=w2=a=1 and Omega=(-1,0,1), alpha=-pi/4, beta=pi/4, K=2-sqrt(2) gives residuals at roundoff and positive Hessian diagonal. Checked CHECK.py source for 450 bounded tests; did not mistake its output for proof.
residual_risks: The global threshold is an infimum of locally stable equilibria; nothing is proved about global basins or nonprincipal lock uniqueness. The finite 450-case program is supplementary.
